title: Pronouns and ongoing actions
goal: Replace nouns with pronouns, describe your daily routine, and say what you (and others) are doing right now.

grammar.p: Direct object (WHAT or WHOM): *me, te, lo, la, nos, los, las*. Use *lo/la/los/las* for things and people, matching gender and number: *el celular → lo*, *las llaves → las*. Indirect object (TO/FOR whom): *me, te, le, nos, les*, with verbs like *dar, decir, mandar, prestar, explicar, preguntar, pedir*. The pronoun goes BEFORE a conjugated verb. Spanish often keeps the indirect pronoun even when the person is named: *Le di el regalo a mi mamá.* In Latin America, use *lo/la* (not *le*) for 'him/her' as a direct object: *Lo vi ayer.*
ex: ¿El celular? No lo encuentro.
The cell phone? I can't find it.
Las llaves las tengo yo.
I've got the keys.
Mi hermano me mandó un mensaje.
My brother sent me a message.
Le expliqué el problema a mi jefe.
I explained the problem to my boss.

grammar.h: Two pronouns together: se lo, me la, te los
grammar.p: When you use both, the indirect (person) comes first, then the direct (thing): *me lo, te la, nos los*. If both start with *l*, *le* or *les* changes to *se*: never *le lo*, always *se lo*. *Se* can mean to him, to her, to you (usted), to them, or to you all; add *a él / a ella / a usted* if you need to be clear.
ex: ¿Me prestas tu carro? —Sí, te lo presto.
Will you lend me your car? —Yes, I'll lend it to you.
¿Le diste el libro a Pedro? —Sí, se lo di.
Did you give the book to Pedro? —Yes, I gave it to him.
Las fotos se las mandé a mis papás.
I sent the photos to my parents.

grammar.h: Reflexive verbs and the daily routine
grammar.p: Reflexive verbs carry a pronoun that matches the subject: *me, te, se, nos, se*. *Levantarse*: *me levanto, te levantas, se levanta, nos levantamos, se levantan*. Many routine verbs work this way: *despertarse (me despierto), acostarse (me acuesto), vestirse (me visto), bañarse, lavarse los dientes, sentirse (me siento)*. With body parts and clothes, Spanish uses *el/la*, not 'my': *Me lavo las manos.* Compare: *Me despierto* (I wake up) vs. *Mi mamá me despierta* (My mom wakes me up). In Mexico, *bañarse* is the everyday word for taking a shower.
ex: Me levanto a las seis y me baño.
I get up at six and take a shower.
Los niños se acuestan a las nueve.
The kids go to bed at nine.
¿Cómo te sientes hoy?
How are you feeling today?

grammar.h: Right now and still: estar + gerund, seguir + gerund
grammar.p: For an action in progress right now: *estar* + gerund. Gerunds: *-ar → -ando* (trabajando), *-er/-ir → -iendo* (comiendo, viviendo). Spelling and stem changes: *leyendo, oyendo, trayendo, durmiendo, diciendo, pidiendo, sintiendo, viniendo*. For 'still / keep on doing': *seguir* + gerund (*sigo, sigues, sigue, seguimos, siguen*): *Sigue lloviendo* = It's still raining.
ex: Estoy manejando, te llamo después.
I'm driving, I'll call you later.
El bebé está durmiendo.
The baby is sleeping.
Mi papá sigue trabajando a los setenta años.
My dad is still working at seventy.

grammar.p: Before a conjugated verb: *Lo veo.* With an infinitive or a gerund you have TWO correct choices: before the conjugated verb, or attached to the end: *Lo voy a llamar = Voy a llamarlo*; *Me estoy vistiendo = Estoy vistiéndome*. Never in the middle (*voy a lo llamar* is wrong). With an affirmative command the pronoun must be attached: *Dime. Dámelo. Dígame.* When attaching adds syllables, write an accent to keep the stress where it was: *haciendo → haciéndolo*, *da → dámelo*. Attaching ONE pronoun to an infinitive needs no accent (*llamarlo, verte*), but two pronouns do (*devolvértelo*).
ex: Te voy a llamar mañana. / Voy a llamarte mañana.
I'm going to call you tomorrow.
Lo estoy haciendo. / Estoy haciéndolo.
I'm doing it.
¿Tu libro? Te lo quiero devolver. / Quiero devolvértelo.
Your book? I want to give it back to you.
Dime la verdad.
Tell me the truth.

vocab: right now / in a little bit (Mexico)
phrases: I'm driving, I'll call you later.
Will you lend it to me?
I'll give it back to you tomorrow.
Tell me. / How can I help you? (usted)
What time do you go to bed?

items.q: ¿Dónde está mi celular? No ___ veo.
items.qen: Where's my cell phone? I don't see it.
items.why: El celular is masculine singular → lo.

items.q: ¿Tienes las llaves? —Sí, ___ tengo aquí.
items.qen: Do you have the keys? —Yes, I have them here.
items.why: Las llaves is feminine plural → las.

items.q: ¿Compraste la leche? —Sí, ___ compré esta mañana.
items.qen: Did you buy the milk? —Yes, I bought it this morning.
items.why: La leche is feminine singular → la.

items.q: Ayer ___ di un regalo a mi mamá.
items.qen: Yesterday I gave my mom a gift.
items.why: To my mom = indirect object → le. 'Se' only replaces le when another pronoun (lo/la) follows.

items.q: Mis hijos siempre ___ piden dinero.
items.qen: My kids always ask me for money.
items.why: 'Ask me' → indirect object pronoun me, placed before the verb.

items.q: ¿Le diste el libro a Pedro? —Sí, ya ___ di.
items.qen: Did you give the book to Pedro? —Yes, I already gave it to him.
items.why: Le + lo → se lo (le becomes se before lo). El libro is masculine → lo.

items.q: ¿Me prestas tu pluma? —Sí, ___ presto.
items.qen: Will you lend me your pen? —Yes, I'll lend it to you.
items.why: To you (tú) = te; la pluma is feminine = la → te la.

items.q: ¿Les mandaste las fotos a tus papás? —Sí, ___ mandé anoche.
items.qen: Did you send the photos to your parents? —Yes, I sent them to them last night.
items.why: Les + las → se las. Las fotos is feminine plural.

items.q: Todos los días ___ levanto a las seis.
items.qen: Every day I get up at six.
items.why: Reflexive pronoun matches the subject: yo → me levanto.

items.q: Los niños ___ acuestan a las nueve.
items.qen: The kids go to bed at nine.
items.why: Ellos → reflexive se: se acuestan.

items.q: En este momento mi esposa ___.
items.qen: My wife is taking a shower right now.
items.why: In progress right now → estar + gerund, and bañarse needs se: se está bañando. 'Está bañando' without se means she is bathing someone else.

items.q: El bebé está ___.
items.why: Dormir changes o → u in the gerund: durmiendo.

items.q: ¿Qué estás ___?
items.why: Leer → leyendo (the i becomes y between vowels).

items.q: Mi papá ___ trabajando a los setenta años.
items.qen: My dad is still working at seventy.
items.why: Seguir + gerund = still doing. Él → sigue (with u to keep the hard g sound).

items.q: How do you say 'I'm going to call him tomorrow'?
items.why: The pronoun goes before the conjugated verb (Lo voy a llamar) or attached to the infinitive (voy a llamarlo) — never in the middle or as a separate word after the infinitive.

items.q: Which is spelled correctly? ('I'm doing it.')
items.why: Attaching lo adds a syllable, so the stress (on -cien-) is now third from the end and needs a written accent: haciéndolo.

items.q: Your friend is holding your phone. Tell him: 'Give it to me.'
items.why: Affirmative command: pronouns are attached, indirect before direct, with an accent: dámelo.

items.q: How do you say 'I feel tired'?
items.why: Sentirse is reflexive and stem-changing (e → ie): me siento.

items.q: ¿La receta? Mi mamá ___ va a mandar mañana.
items.qen: The recipe? My mom is going to send it to me tomorrow.
items.why: To me = me, la receta = la; indirect first → me la.

items.q: Disculpe, señor, ¿___ puedo hacer una pregunta?
items.qen: Excuse me, sir, may I ask you a question?
items.why: Hacer una pregunta A usted → indirect object le.

items.q: ¿Viste a Carlos? —Sí, ___ vi en el gimnasio.
items.en: Did you see Carlos? —Yes, I saw him at the gym.
items.why: Carlos is the direct object, masculine → lo (standard in Latin America).

items.q: ¿Dónde pusiste las tazas? —___ puse en la mesa.
items.en: Where did you put the cups? —I put them on the table.
items.why: Las tazas is feminine plural → las.

items.q: Mi hermano ___ escribió una carta a mi abuela.
items.en: My brother wrote a letter to my grandmother.
items.why: A mi abuela is the indirect object → le (Spanish keeps le even when the person is named).

items.q: ¿Me ayudas? —Claro, ___ ayudo.
items.en: Will you help me? —Sure, I'll help you.
items.why: You (tú) as an object → te.

items.q: ¿Les explicaste el plan a los niños? —Sí, ya ___ expliqué.
items.en: Did you explain the plan to the kids? —Yes, I already explained it to them.
items.why: Les + lo → se lo. El plan is masculine singular.

items.q: Necesito tu carro mañana. ¿___ prestas?
items.en: I need your car tomorrow. Will you lend it to me?
items.why: To me = me, el carro = lo → me lo.

items.q: Todos los días ___ despierto a las cinco y media.
items.en: Every day I wake up at five thirty.
items.why: Despertarse, yo → me despierto.

items.q: Mis hijos ___ los dientes después de comer.
items.en: My kids brush their teeth after eating.
items.why: Ellos → se lavan. Spanish uses los dientes, not 'their teeth'.

items.q: Anoche ___ muy tarde.
items.en: Last night I went to bed very late.
items.why: Anoche → preterite; yo → me acosté (no stem change in the preterite).

items.q: ¿A qué hora ___ tú normalmente?
items.en: What time do you usually get up?
items.why: Tú → te levantas.

items.q: No puedo hablar ahora, ___ manejando.
items.en: I can't talk now, I'm driving.
items.why: In progress → estar + gerund; yo → estoy.

items.q: Los niños están ___ en el parque.
items.en: The kids are playing in the park.
items.why: -ar verb → -ando: jugando.

items.q: Mi abuela está ___ el periódico.
items.en: My grandmother is reading the newspaper.
items.why: Leer → leyendo.

items.q: Perdón, ¿qué me estás ___?
items.en: Sorry, what are you telling me?
items.why: Decir has the gerund diciendo (e → i).

items.q: Mi mamá ___ trabajando en la misma tienda.
items.en: My mom is still working at the same store.
items.why: Seguir + gerund = still doing; ella → sigue.

items.q: Nosotros ___ viviendo en el mismo apartamento.
items.en: We're still living in the same apartment.
items.why: Nosotros → seguimos (no stem change in the nosotros form).

items.q: Tengo que llamar a mi hermana. Voy a ___ esta noche.
items.en: I have to call my sister. I'm going to call her tonight.
items.why: After 'voy a' the pronoun attaches to the infinitive: llamarla (no accent needed).

items.q: ¿El informe? Estoy ___ ahora mismo.
items.en: The report? I'm writing it right now.
items.why: Pronoun attached to the gerund, with an accent to keep the stress: escribiéndolo.

items.q: Si tienes una pregunta, ___.
items.en: If you have a question, tell me.
items.why: Affirmative tú command + attached pronoun: dime.

items.q: ¿La tarea? No ___ hoy.
items.en: The homework? I can't finish it today.
items.why: Both positions are correct: la puedo terminar = puedo terminarla.

My brother sent me a message yesterday.

You're going to send it to me tonight.

My mom wakes me up at six.

turns.en: Hey, do you still have my umbrella?

turns.why: To you (tú) = te; el paraguas is masculine = lo → te lo devuelvo.

turns.es: Perfecto. ¿Y me puedes prestar tu cargador? Mi celular se está descargando.
turns.en: Perfect. And can you lend me your charger? My phone is running out of battery.

turns.why: I lend it to you (tú) → te lo presto. 'Se lo' would be usted or him/her, wrong for a friend.

turns.en: Hi, son. What are you doing?

turns.why: Right now → estar + gerund, yo form: estoy cocinando.
The kids (ellos) → se están bañando. 'Me estoy' is about you; the other mixes past with mañana.

turns.es: Bueno, no te quito más tiempo. Te llamo mañana.
turns.en: Okay, I won't take up any more of your time. I'll call you tomorrow.

turns.es: Te ves cansado. ¿A qué hora te levantaste hoy?
turns.en: You look tired. What time did you get up today?

opts: Me levanté a las cuatro y media.
Te levantaste a las cuatro y media.
Me levanto a las cuatro y media ayer.
turns.why: About yourself, finished today → preterite: me levanté.

turns.es: ¡Qué temprano! ¿Y a qué hora te acuestas normalmente?
turns.en: So early! And what time do you usually go to bed?

opts: Normalmente me acosté a las once.
Normalmente se acuesta a las once.
Normalmente me acuesto a las once.
turns.why: A habit → present; yo → me acuesto (o → ue).

turns.en: You need to sleep more, my friend.

items.title: Helping an older woman on the street

turns.es: Disculpe, joven, ¿me puede ayudar? Estoy buscando una farmacia.
turns.en: Excuse me, young man, can you help me? I'm looking for a pharmacy.

turns.why: An older stranger → usted: está buscando. The third repeats the object with a pronoun, which is wrong here.

turns.es: La que está en la calle Ashland. Me dijeron que está cerca. ¿Me puede escribir la dirección? No veo bien.
turns.en: The one on Ashland Street. They told me it's close. Can you write the address down for me? I don't see well.

turns.why: To her (usted) = le → se before la; la dirección = la → se la escribo.

turns.es: Muchas gracias, joven. Es usted muy amable.
turns.en: Thank you very much, young man. You're very kind.
Did you get to the party yet?

opts: No, sigo manejando. Hay mucho tráfico.
No, sigue manejando. Hay mucho tráfico.
No, sigo manejado. Hay mucho tráfico.
turns.why: Still driving → seguir + gerund, yo form: sigo manejando.

turns.es: Bueno. ¿Me puedes comprar hielo en el camino?
turns.en: Okay. Can you buy me some ice on the way?

turns.why: For you (tú) = te; el hielo is masculine = lo → te lo compro.

turns.en: Thanks! I'll wait for you here.

turns.es: ¿Ya le diste el regalo a Rosa?
turns.en: Did you already give Rosa the gift?

opts: No, le lo voy a dar mañana.
No, se la voy a dar mañana.
No, se lo voy a dar mañana.
turns.why: Le + lo → se lo; el regalo is masculine → se lo voy a dar.

turns.en: And the card? Did you sign it yet?

turns.why: La tarjeta is feminine → la; a finished action → firmé.

turns.en: Perfect. She's going to love it.

roleplay.title: Sunday phone call with a friend
roleplay.setup: Your friend Roberto calls on a Sunday morning while you are busy at home. Tell him what you're doing, talk about your routines, and sort out lending him something.
roleplay.persona: You play Roberto, 40, a friend of the learner, originally from Puebla, Mexico, now an accountant in Chicago. Use tú. Speak in clear, everyday sentences built around this level's grammar: direct/indirect object pronouns, double pronouns (te lo, se la), reflexive daily-routine verbs, estar + gerund, seguir + gerund, and pronouns attached to infinitives, gerunds and simple tú commands (dime, pásamelo). You may use present, preterite, imperfect, ir a + infinitive and the present perfect, but avoid the subjunctive. Facts: you are calling because you are painting your living room and need to borrow a ladder (la escalera) and a drill (el taladro); you already asked your brother but he lent his to someone else; you get up at 5:30 every day, even on weekends, and you're still working at the same firm after ten years. Reveal these only when asked. Ask the learner what he is doing right now, what time he got up, and whether he can lend you the ladder. If he agrees, ask when he can bring it to you (expect answers like 'te la llevo esta tarde' / 'te la puedo llevar…'). React naturally to pronoun mistakes, e.g. '¿La escalera? ¿Me la vas a traer?'.
goals: Tell him what you are doing right now (estar + gerund)
Tell him what time you got up and what you usually do on Sundays
Find out why he is calling and what he needs
Agree to lend him the ladder and say when you'll bring it, using a pronoun (te la…)
Ask what he has been doing at work lately (sigue trabajando…)

roleplay.title: Helping a neighbor with packages
roleplay.setup: Doña Lupe, an older neighbor, has several packages delivered to the lobby and asks you for help. Use usted with her.
roleplay.persona: You play Doña Lupe, 76, a retired seamstress from Zacatecas, Mexico, who lives alone on the fourth floor. Polite and grateful; use usted with the learner and expect usted back (react with gentle surprise if he uses tú). Use this level's grammar: object pronouns and double pronouns (se lo, se las), reflexive verbs, estar + gerund, seguir + gerund. Avoid the subjunctive. Facts to reveal only when asked: there are three boxes (las cajas) and one big bag; the boxes have plates and a new blanket (una cobija) that her daughter sent her from Zacatecas; her daughter is sending her things because she is moving to Chicago next month; Doña Lupe's knee still hurts (le sigue doliendo la rodilla), so she can't carry heavy things; she goes to bed early and gets up at six to pray and make coffee. Ask the learner to carry the boxes up for her and where he is going to leave them. Accept answers like 'Se las subo ahorita' or 'Se las voy a dejar en la cocina'.
roleplay.opening: Ay, joven, buenas tardes. ¿Me puede ayudar con estas cajas, por favor?
goals: Offer to carry the boxes up, using a double pronoun (se las…)
Ask what is in the boxes and who sent them
Ask how she is feeling and whether her knee still hurts
Tell her where you are going to leave the boxes
Ask about her daily routine (what time she gets up / goes to bed)
